name: Add Interactions
gate: after build CSS (static render must match Paper first)
instruction: Wire interactive behaviors and motion. Paper is static and drops CSS transition and animation, so it shows resting states plus, where motion matters, a frame strip. Behaviors (hover, click, expand, keyboard) come from {spec}. Motion comes from the frame strip drawn for the element, else from {spec}.

process.instruction: Read the section's interactions from {spec} (a spec file under the project's doc root, or the tracking issue). Each row has: Trigger, Behavior, Reduced motion fallback. If {spec} has no interaction table, ask once for the source rather than inventing behavior.

process.step: I2 - Read the motion frame strips
process.instruction: Look on the artboard (and the page's motion area, if any) for a frame strip next to each interactive element: Start, Mid and End frames captioned with duration, curve and motion token names, sometimes with a curve plot. Extract the frames' styles with get_computed_styles like any other node. The differences between Start and End are the properties that animate; the captions give duration and easing.
rules: Use the project's motion tokens for duration and easing when the caption names one; otherwise add a token.
If an element animates in code but has no strip and no spec row, ask once; do not invent motion.
Never write transition, animation or @keyframes back into Paper (write_html or update_styles); Paper drops them. If Paper needs a motion change, draw or update the frame strip instead.

process.instruction: For each interaction that changes visible content (expand/collapse, tab switch, filter, toggle), add the minimal local state in the {framework} idiom (see the Framework branches table in ../reference/project-conventions.md). One state variable per independent toggle.

Add click and keydown handlers in the {framework} idiom. Every interactive element must be a button (or the project's button component, or have role='button' + tabindex). Keyboard support: Enter/Space to activate, Escape to close expanded content, Tab to traverse.
keyboard_rules: Every clickable element is a <button> with type='button', or the project's button component
Expanded content collapses on Escape and returns focus to the trigger
The focus ring uses the project's focus token ({prefix}focus-ring or its equivalent)

process.instruction: Add :hover, :focus-visible and state-driven class toggles to the CSS, with the motion from I2.
hover_rules: Hover effects from the spec's interaction table (shadow intensify, lift, background change)
transition lists the specific properties that differ between the strip's Start and End frames, with the strip's duration and curve tokens
reduced_motion_rules: Or override them in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) to remove transform, keep opacity
If the project has a shared reduced-motion stylesheet or utility, use it instead of repeating rules

process.instruction: If the strip or {spec} shows the section or its children entering (fade, slide, stagger), use the project's existing entrance mechanism (a reveal component, directive or utility class) if it has one; find it in {component_dir}. Otherwise implement it with CSS and an IntersectionObserver in the {framework} idiom, with a reduced-motion fallback. Skip this step when nothing enters.

interaction_checklist.instruction: After wiring all interactions, verify against the spec table and the strips. For each row:
checks: Trigger: is the element interactive (button, not div)?
Behavior: does the state change produce the described visual change?
Motion: do duration, curve and animated properties match the frame strip captions?
Reduced motion: is there a fallback that removes animation but preserves the state change?
Keyboard: can the interaction be triggered with keyboard alone?
